approach: Add a `Priority` enum (High, Normal, Low; derive Ord with High first) to plan.rs with `Priority::from_text` reading a case-insensitive `Priority: <level>` line, and a `priority` field on `PlanEntry` (default Normal in `bare`). `Plan::build` sorts each ready wave by `(priority, rung, age)`; dependency waves are untouched, so dependencies still win. `reading::plan_entry` sets the priority from the request text. `JobLine` gains a `priority` string, filled in `status::job_line` from the same parser. `display::plan` prints a `priority` line per item, and status open/recent lines get a ` · priority X` suffix. Add tests, a CHANGELOG entry and a decisions.md entry.

decisions.choice: Priority is the first sort key within a ready wave: (priority, rung, age). The wave loop is unchanged, so dependencies come first.
decisions.reason: Smallest change, and it meets 'priority before age' while keeping dependency order. A high item that depends on an older normal one is not ready until that one is done.

rejected.option: Priority above rung and also lifting dependencies of a high item
rejected.why: Changes dependency semantics and is out of scope; a transitive boost can be a later change.
The cutover request would still sit behind older higher-rung work; the request asks for priority before age, and the reading puts it first.

decisions.choice: Read priority from a 'Priority: <level>' line in the request text, via one shared parser `Priority::from_text` in plan.rs used by plan_entry and status.
decisions.reason: Needs no new command or stored field; the request text is already the record. One parser keeps plan and status consistent.

rejected.option: A command-set field stored in records
rejected.why: Needs a new command and record schema; out of scope. Recorded in decisions.md as the alternative.

decisions.choice: Closed set high/normal/low; an unknown level or missing line gives Normal. The first valid Priority line wins.
decisions.reason: A typo must not reorder the queue; the default preserves today's order.

files.purpose: Priority enum and parser, PlanEntry.priority (bare = Normal), sort key (priority, rung, age), module doc, unit tests.
plan_entry sets entry.priority from the request text; test on the text.
JobLine gains priority (string), filled in job_line from the request text.
Plan item shows a priority line; status open/recent lines show a priority suffix; display test.
Plan display test covers the priority line and a high item drained first.
Decision entry: alternatives and the cutover motivation.

steps: Read the tails of CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md for the format and the next decision number.

In plan.rs add `Priority` (High, Normal, Low; derive Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize with kebab-case; `as_str`; `from_text(&str)`). Add `pub priority: Priority` to PlanEntry and set Normal in `bare`. Change the sort to `ready.sort_by_key(|(age, e)| (e.priority, e.rung, *age))`. Update the module doc Order bullet.
Add plan.rs tests: high newest first, dependency beats priority, no-priority order unchanged, low last, parser cases.
In reading.rs plan_entry set `entry.priority = Priority::from_text(text)`; add a test.
In status.rs add `priority: String` to JobLine and set it in job_line from `job.request` text.
In display.rs add a `priority` line in `entry_lines` and a priority suffix on the status open and recent lines; add a test.
Extend tests/drain.rs plan display test with a high item and the priority needles.
Add the CHANGELOG entry and the decisions.md entry.
Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Existing tests that assert exact status or plan output could break.
risks.mitigation: Print the priority as a separate ' · priority X' suffix after the plan suffix and a separate 'priority' line in plan; run the full cargo test.

risks.risk: The derived Ord puts the wrong end first.
risks.mitigation: Priority derives Ord with variants in the order High, Normal, Low, and a test asserts high before normal before low.

risks.risk: Request prose containing 'priority' reorders the queue by accident.
risks.mitigation: Only an exact level word after 'Priority:' on a line that starts with it counts; anything else is Normal; tested.

risks.risk: PlanEntry struct literals elsewhere break when a field is added.
risks.mitigation: Use `..PlanEntry::bare` in new test literals; the existing literals already use it, and compile errors will show any exceptions.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in plan.rs: build entries [n1,n2,n3 normal, h high (newest)], all the same rung and no dependencies; assert Plan::build order starts with h.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the priority sort key the newer high entry is ordered last and the assertion on order[0] fails.

demonstrations.method: Unit test: h is high and depends_on n1 (normal, older); also an unrelated normal n2. Assert position(n1) < position(h).
demonstrations.observes: n1 is before h; h is not before its dependency.
demonstrations.fails_without: If priority overrode dependencies, h (high, depends on older normal n1) would come before n1 and the test fails.

demonstrations.method: New plan.rs test: entries with no priority and different rungs and ages; assert the order equals the expected rung-then-age order. The existing plan tests and the drain.rs integration tests run unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: Order is rung then age; all tests pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the sort changed the default order, the no-priority test would see a different rung-then-age order, and the existing tests would fail.

demonstrations.method: In tests/drain.rs, extend the plan display test with a high entry and assert text contains 'priority    high' and 'priority    normal'. In display.rs tests, build a JobLine with priority 'high' and assert the status open-line helper output contains 'priority high'.
demonstrations.observes: The plan output has a priority line per item; the status line shows the priority.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the display change the 'priority' needles are absent and the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Tests in plan.rs for `Priority::from_text` ('Priority: high', 'priority: HIGH', an indented line, a text without the line, 'Priority: urgent' as Normal) and in reading.rs for plan_entry on a job whose request text has the line.
demonstrations.observes: High for the line in any case; Normal otherwise.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the parser every request reads as normal and the high-case assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Read the module doc. It states that the order is priority, then rung, then age, with dependencies first. Check with git diff.
demonstrations.observes: The 'Order.' bullet names priority, rung, age and dependencies first.
A CHANGELOG entry for request priority; a decisions.md entry giving the words-in-request versus command-field alternatives and the 2026-10-24 records-history cutover (D111 job 7) motivation.
